<!-- GitHub Pages serves docs/404.html for any missing page. The log below reads like
     Stata's Results window; the script fills in the path the visitor asked for, and the
     prompt at the bottom runs on the Stata console in html/site.html. -->

```{=html}
<div class="stata-log" role="group" aria-label="Stata output: the page was not found"><span>. use "<span class="nf-path">/this-page</span>", clear</span>
<span class="stata-err">file <span class="nf-path">/this-page</span>.dta not found</span>
<span class="stata-err">r(601);</span>

<span class="stata-note">. * Probably a moved page or a typo in the link. Try one of these:</span>

<a href="/">. view browse "/"</a>            <span class="stata-note">// home</span>
<a href="/research/">. view browse "/research"</a>    <span class="stata-note">// papers</span>
<a href="/teaching/">. view browse "/teaching"</a>    <span class="stata-note">// courses</span>
<a href="/cv/">. view browse "/cv"</a>
<a href="/blog/">. view browse "/blog"</a>

<span class="stata-note">. * Or type a command below. Start with: help</span>
<div class="stata-out" aria-live="polite"></div><form class="stata-prompt" autocomplete="off"><label for="stata-cmd">.</label> <input id="stata-cmd" type="text" spellcheck="false" autocapitalize="off" enterkeyhint="go" aria-label="Stata command"></form></div>
<script>
// Fill in the path the visitor asked for. The prompt itself is wired in html/site.html.
(() => {
  let p = location.pathname;
  try { p = decodeURI(p); } catch (e) {}
  p = p.replace(/(\/index)?\.html$/, '').replace(/\/+$/, '') || '/';
  document.querySelectorAll('.nf-path').forEach(el => { el.textContent = p; });
})();
</script>
```

::: {.nf-help}
If a link on this site brought you here, please tell me so I can fix it: rrodriguezramirez \[at\] g \[dot\] harvard \[dot\] edu.
:::
